Definition: from θράω (to sit); a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power or (concretely) a potentate:--seat, throne.
BiblicalUsage: thrónos is the word the Bible uses when it means a throne. In Matthew 5:34, it is God's throne. The word turns up 51 times, and each time it points to the same reality.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that the throne that matters is not an earthly seat of power but the throne of the God who reigns for ever. That is why I read the passages around thrónos slowly, instead of hurrying past.
